working_definition: T4b is one of four directional subtypes (a–d) of T4 neurons in the Drosophila optic lobe. It is a columnar, ON-pathway, direction-selective neuron whose dendrites arborise in medulla layer M10 and whose axon terminals project specifically to lobula plate layer 2 (layer b). The four T4 subtypes encode cardinal directions of visual motion; T4b encodes the diagonal back-to-front direction read out in lobula plate layer 2.

best_match.fbbt_definition: T4 neuron with its lobula plate arbor in layer 2 (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989). It responds to motion in a diagonal back-to-front direction (Henning et al., 2022).

justification: FBbt:00003733 'T4b neuron' is defined as the T4 subtype with its lobula plate arbor in layer 2 that responds to diagonal back-to-front motion (Fischbach and Dittrich 1989; Henning et al. 2022). The atlas cluster 'T4b' is defined identically: a T4 (ON-pathway) columnar optic lobe neuron whose axon terminals target lobula plate layer b (layer 2) and which encodes the corresponding cardinal direction of motion. The label, layer specificity, and directional tuning all match precisely. The FBbt term is not obsolete and is a direct subtype of T4 neuron (FBbt:00003731). FBbt further sub-divides T4b into T4bi (FBbt:00052243) and T4bii (FBbt:00052244) based on finer diagonal direction sub-tuning (downward vs upward back-to-front), but the atlas cluster 'T4b' does not resolve to that level of granularity; the cluster maps to the T4b level, not the sub-sub-types.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: T neuron with its cell body posterior to the lobula plate and a cell body fiber that projects through the lobula plate and via the second optic chiasma, with little or no arborization, to medulla layer 10 (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Shinomiya et al., 2019). It forms a fine arborization in medulla layers M9 and M10 and its axon then doubles back across the second optic chiasma to form bleb-type arborizations in a single layer of the lobula plate (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Shinomiya et al., 2019). It is a cholinergic neuron (Mauss et al., 2014; Shinomiya et al., 2014). There are a large number of these cells, which are generated from neuroblasts that amplify by symmetric division (type III) before generating the T4 (and T5) neurons (Mora et al., 2018).
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Parent term covering all four T4 subtypes (a–d); the cluster 'T4b' is specifically the layer-2 subtype. Using the parent would be a broad match and would lose the defining layer-identity information that is central to this cluster's annotation.
